You use the simple past tense to talk about situations that started and finished at a specific time in the past.
To make affirmative sentence in simple past, you should use verbs in past form:
Subject + verb in past form + complement.

Ada Lovelace invented the first computer program in 1843.
Herman Hollerith introduced the concept of storing data in the 1880's.
Data storage devices became less expensive by the 1960's.
Verbs in past are classified in regular and irregular:
The past form of regular verbs is simple, you just need to add -d, -ed, or -ied at the end of the verb.

create→ created
invent → invented
study → studied
Irregular verbs can change in different forms, you need to practice and memorize them.

keep → kept
think → thought
become → became
To make negative statements in past simple with the verb to be, you use the following structure:

Ada Lovelace wasn't the first person that invented a computer program.
Computer programs weren't common in the XIX century.

When you make negative statements with other verbs; you don't have to use the past form of the verb but the infinitive form. Also, you need to include the auxiliary did in negative before the main verb:
Subject + didn't + verb in infinitive + complement.

Herman Hollerith didn't introduce the concept of storing data in the 1880's.
Data storage devices didn't become less expensive by the 1960's.
To make questions in past simple with the verb to be, you use the following structure:

Was Ada Lovelace the first person that invented a computer program?
Were computer programs common in the XIX century?
When you ask questions with other verbs; you don't have to use the past form of the verb but the infinitive form. Also, you need to include the auxiliary did at the beginning of the question:
Did + subject + verb in infinitive+ complement?

Did Herman Hollerith introduce the concept of storing data in the 1880's?
Did data storage devices become less expensive by the 1960's?
You can also use WH words in questions when you are asking for specific information:

Who was Adam Lovelace?
Why were computers programs more common in the XX century?
Why did data storage devices become less expensive by the 1960's?
Programming devices existed since very early times but it wasn't until the mid-nineteenth century that Ada Lovelace invented the first computer program.

But, when did software engineering truly emerge? At the beginning of the XX century, there were many people dedicated to create and improve computer systems, however, this field didn't emerge as a profession until the 60's.

A paragraph is a group of sentences connected by the logic of a single idea. This way, the sentences within the paragraph develop just one main idea. A paragraph should have three essential parts: a topic sentence, some supporting sentences, and a concluding sentence. </br>Take a look at the following chart:

As you know, the intention of this blog is to post information about technology, computing systems, and programming languages. Today, I want to focus on the history of software and some related information to software engineering. </br>
Programming devices existed since very early times but it wasn't until the mid-nineteenth century that Ada Lovelace invented the first computer program. Years later, Herman Hollerith introduced the concept of storing data and IBM launched the first electronic computer in the late 1940's.

But, when did software engineering truly emerge? At the beginning of the XX century, there were many people dedicated to create and improve computer systems, however, this field didn't emerge as a profession until the 60's. From that time on, software developers aimed and still aim to guarantee the stability, speed, usability, testability, readability, size, cost, and security of computer programs.
</br>The evolution of this field is remarkable in different areas. First of all, processes, as we may know, are now fundamental in software engineering and they led to all the progress that we can see now in programming languages, data storage devices or computer terminals. On another note, we can notice how the cost of software and hardware changed with the evolution of computer programming. By the late 60's, it was really expensive to afford mainframes and support staff, but the boom of computers made these machines cheaper and more companies are now able to support larger software projects.

Another interesting fact is the rise of the internet, thanks to the creation of the web browser in the early 90's. This led to a fast growth in the demand for international information, and improvements in the email systems, network connections, and media display and storage were necessary.</br>
Nowadays, all the rapid changes in technology, the current tendency in software development, is creating programs and apps for smaller companies, and programmers are constantly developing agile lightweight methodologies, and alternative approaches to software calculations and information storage.
